item.description:
Git status on the Mac, move and copy in fewer steps, and swipe on the iPad and the iPhone.
### New - **Git status on the Mac:** in a git repository each file and folder shows its state on its icon: a dot for modified, a ring for new, a diamond for a conflict, and an ignored item is dimmed. A folder shows what it holds, so you can follow the changes down the tree. The Git column says it in words and sorts the changes to the top, the status bar shows the branch and how many commits are to push and to pull, and the sidebar marks each repository. Treewise only reads your repositories and never changes them. It uses the git of Apple's Command Line Tools or Homebrew; without one, Settings > General offers Install…, and Show Git status there turns it off. - **Move to and Copy to with the folders you use:** the context menu (and on the Mac also the Edit menu) offers Move to and Copy to with the last five folders you moved or copied something into, by any way, at the top, then your favorites, then Choose Folder… to pick any other. On the iPad they are now there at every width, as on the iPhone. - **Swipe a row on the iPad and the iPhone:** swipe left for Move to Trash, which a full swipe does at once, and More… with Share, Rename and the rest; swipe right for Cut, which a full swipe does at once, and Copy.
### Improved - **Clearer file icons on the iPad and the iPhone:** each file shows its type at a glance, as a page with a coloured label and its extension: red for PDF, green for spreadsheets, blue for documents. Settings > General > File Icons offers two other looks and the system's own icons.
### Fixed - Swiping a favorite away on the iPad or the iPhone, after its location was removed and added again, no longer ends the app. - A folder structure template deleted on the iPad stays deleted. - Move to Trash in On My iPad no longer hangs on iPadOS 27. - A zip with a password is no longer now and then called damaged when you open or extract it on the Mac; Treewise says it needs a password. - On the Mac, the details pane shows Made from for a folder you fill from a template while it is selected, without selecting another first. - On the Mac, a folder in the sidebar shows its disclosure triangle as soon as Treewise makes folders in it, also when it is closed in the tree, and a folder that gained folders while its parent was closed shows it when the parent opens again.

Treewise on the iPad, the iPhone and the iPhone Duo.
### New - **Treewise for iPad, iPhone and iPhone Duo** in the App Store: the same folders, drag and drop, cut and paste, name suggestions and folder structure templates as on the Mac, with your settings shared through your cloud drives. On the iPhone the folder shows as a list; on the iPhone Duo, opened, as a table beside the sidebar.
### Improved - **Whole names suggested:** when the files in a folder have the same text after their date, as `2026-07-12 Texel` and `2026-07-13 Texel`, Suggest Names and Rename with Suggestions now propose that text too, as `2026-07-15 Texel`, instead of leaving a part for you to fill in.

Your folder settings, patterns and templates on every Mac.
### New - **Your settings on every Mac:** the patterns of your folders, your saved patterns and your folder structure templates now follow you to your other Macs, and later your iPad, through your cloud drives: iCloud Drive, Dropbox, Nextcloud and the others in the sidebar. Treewise keeps them in a hidden `.treewise.settings` folder there; nothing goes anywhere else. Change different things on two Macs at once and both changes stay. Settings > General has the switch, which is on. - **Nothing lost when two Macs change the same thing:** the newest change wins, and the one it replaced is kept for 30 days on its Mac, where Settings > General lists it with Restore.

One folder renamed in every year, and a shorter context menu.
### New - **Rename in All Years…** on a folder inside a year's folder, such as `2025/Tax`, gives that folder its new name in every year at once. A sheet shows each year first, leaves out a year that already has a folder with the new name, corrects the template the years were made from, and one Undo takes all of it back. - **A misspelled folder found for you:** with Folder Structure Templates, the bar in a year's folder notices a folder of the year before that is nearly named as one there, such as `Belastingsdienst` beside `Belastingdienst`, and asks which name to keep in every year, or to add it anyway. - **A folder remembers its template:** a folder made from a folder structure template keeps which one, shown as *Made from* in the details pane, with a button to forget it. Rename in All Years and Add to Template then offer that template, also when you have more than one for your years, and a template exported and imported on another Mac is still known as the same one.
### Improved - **A shorter context menu:** it shows only what can be done with what you clicked, and groups compressing, folder structures and Suggest Names in a submenu each, the usual command first.
### Fixed - On a disk that cannot keep Treewise's mark on a folder, such as some USB sticks, a folder's settings in Suggest Names and templates now stay with it when Treewise renames or moves it.

Change a name that already fits from where it is.
### Improved - **Another name for a file that already fits** starts from the name it has, as renaming in Finder does: press Return in Suggest Names and change what you need.

Suggest Names leaves names that already fit alone, and the name add-ons get names that say what they do.
### New - **Date Created and Date Added columns.** Right-click the list's column headers to show them, and sort by either.
### Improved - **Suggest Names on selected files** keeps a name that already fits the pattern; what the add-ons propose for it is still there with the arrows. - **Suggest Names on a folder** proposes names for the files in it, not a new name for the folder. - **The name add-ons are called File Name Patterns** and Advanced File Name Patterns, as they name files. Your patterns, settings and licence carry over. - **Stop ends a copy that waits for a file kept only online** to download, leaving nothing behind.
### Fixed - **⌘-click selects several items** in the list view again; it kept only the item clicked last.

Set up the same folders again in one go: for a new client, a new project or a new year.
### New - **Folder templates.** Save a folder's structure, its folders without their files, as a template, and make it anywhere with New Folders from Template. You see every folder before it is made, folders already there are kept and filled, and one Undo takes them all away again. - **Copy and paste a folder structure** without saving a template: Copy Folder Structure on one folder, Paste Folder Structure… on another. - **Folder names that fill themselves in.** A template's names can hold the year, a number that counts on, today's date or a text you type when you make it. A folder can repeat for each month, quarter or half, so one template makes `01 January` to `12 December`. - **Settings › Templates** to rename, edit, duplicate, import and export your templates. - **The Folder Structure Templates add-on**, free to try for 14 days, makes one template from a year's folder that works for every year. When a new year's folder is empty or lacks folders of the year before, it offers to make them. - **About Treewise** says what Treewise is, with links to the website, the source code and the privacy statement. Help › Acknowledgements lists the licences of the parts it uses.
### Improved - **Faster in large folders.** Suggest Names proposes names in a folder with a thousand files several times faster, and the icon view makes only the thumbnails you see and uses less memory for them. - **Suggest Names says why** it has nothing to propose, in a bar above the list. - **Tidier Settings.** Add-ons are grouped under Names and Folders, every list has a right-click menu, and name patterns can be duplicated. - **The sidebar** shows no disclosure triangle on a folder without subfolders, shows a long name in full when you point at it, and starts at a comfortable width in a new window. - **A narrow list** makes its names narrower first and then scrolls sideways, as Finder does, instead of cutting off columns.
### Fixed - The sidebar shows a new, renamed or removed folder at once, whether Treewise or another app changed it. - After a restart, or a jump to a folder far down a long tree, the sidebar shows that folder in its middle instead of at its edge. - Window Beside on a small screen no longer leaves a window partly off the screen. - The command bar's menus show their icons again on macOS 27. - An item dropped on a sidebar folder that opened while you held it over it lands in that folder. - Compressing two items with the same name from different folders keeps both. - An Undo that cannot be done says so. - Settings › Add-ons no longer shows an add-on twice after it is dragged.

### Added - The Advanced Folder Pattern add-on learns a series that starts again each year from a complete year: where it ends, a list of numbers it skips, and how wide they are written, as `{seq:24:1}` or `{seq:5,10,15,20}`. In a folder per year it can read the names in the same folder a year before, as `Administration/2025/Tax` beside `Administration/2026/Tax`, so a new year's folder gets last year's pattern at once. Settings > Add-ons has Also read names in the same folder a year before, on by default; only names are read. - Halves after an H, as `H1` and `H2`, continue as a series of two.
### Changed - Settings > Add-ons shows each add-on as a card with its licence as a coloured badge and a switch. Selecting a card opens it and folds the others; the list fills the tab and scrolls to the card selected. What an add-on recognizes shows with an example of each field, as `{seq:4}` 1–4, coloured by kind. - Advanced Folder Pattern learns a list from one complete year whose numbers step evenly, as 2, 4, 6, 8, and such a list comes before the months. - The sidebar can be made wider, up to 400 points, and starts at 260. Each window keeps its sidebar's width, also after a restart, and a new window starts at the width last chosen. When the window is made narrower, the sidebar gives way first. The sidebar's button stands at the right over the sidebar, away from the window's buttons.
### Fixed - The Settings window is titled by the tab chosen, instead of Untitled.

### Added - The Advanced Folder Pattern add-on comes with Treewise. It recognizes more in a folder's names than the free add-on: years, quarters after a Q and months after a year that continue a series, and names that follow one of several patterns. Try it for 14 days with Try for 14 Days in Settings > Add-ons or in the overview of proposed names; after that it works with a licence key, entered with Enter Licence Key…. It is not for sale yet. - A licence key can have an end date; Settings then says until when it counts, and how many days are left in its last week. - Settings > Add-ons says what each add-on does and what it recognizes in a folder's names. - `{seq}` takes a range, a list or an open end: `{seq:2-4}`, `{seq:2,4,6,8}`, `{seq:5-}`, and its width by leading zeros or a second colon: `{seq:001-}`, `{seq:5-:3}`. - `{year:yy}` writes the year in two digits, `{folder:2}` is the folder above the one that holds the file, and `:lower`, `:upper` and `:title` write a field's text in small letters, capitals or with a capital at each word.
### Changed - A name fits a pattern with `{seq}` only when its number is one the series can give, so `Q5` no longer fits `Q{seq:4}`. - The overview says when a folder has too few names to recognize a pattern in: it needs at least 3.
### Fixed - The buttons at the foot of the overview of proposed names have room around them again, instead of touching the window's edge.

### Added - Extract All… unpacks zip, tar, `.tar.gz`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.xz`, 7z, rar, iso, cpio and xar archives to a new folder, from the command bar, the context menu and the File menu. Nothing lands in the destination unless the whole archive extracted. - Compress to ZIP puts an archive next to the selection and starts renaming it; Compress to also makes 7z and `.tar.gz` files. A zip or 7z leaves out `__MACOSX`, `._` files, `.DS_Store` and extended attributes. - Suggest Names for Whole Folder… in the context menu and the File menu, for a folder so full that a right click always lands on a file. - A double click opens an archive as a folder, and the sidebar's tree unfolds it. Inside it you can browse, sort, search, preview with Quick Look and copy or drag files out; Extract All extracts that archive. Zip, tar and 7z archives can be changed like a folder: add, replace, rename, move, copy, make folders and delete, with undo. A failed change leaves the archive as it was, and the first change puts a copy of the original in the Trash. Rar, iso, cpio and xar stay read-only. - The sidebar's tree opens down to the folder or archive a tab shows; Settings can turn this off. - A Go menu with Back, Forward and Enclosing Folder, as in Finder. - Edit > Spelling and Grammar checks the spelling of a name you are typing; checking while typing is off until you turn it on.
### Changed - Treewise's windows, menus, toolbar, Settings and everything in them are built the way Mac apps build them, which keeps a menu held open while a change ends from closing Treewise on macOS 26. - Settings are laid out as other Mac apps lay out theirs: labels on the left, checkboxes and menus on the right. - Treewise always opens again with the windows and tabs it had when it quit, whatever the system's setting for keeping windows says. - On macOS 26 the progress panel and the badge on a drag stand on Liquid Glass.
### Fixed - The first window opens on the main screen, not on the screen another display happened to give it. - Ending a drag over the sidebar no longer closes Treewise. - A change to a folder made while Treewise was reading it shows up, and an older reading no longer replaces a newer one. - Renaming no longer offers one-time codes from AutoFill, which on macOS 26 could take the keyboard away from the name, so that ⌥Esc and Escape seemed to do nothing. - A new archive, an extracted folder, a new folder and a renamed item are scrolled into view, also when sorting puts them far from where you were working.
